title.zh: 卷一百一十六 載記第十六 姚弋仲 姚襄 姚萇
title.en: Volume 116 Records 16: Yao Yizhong; Yao Xiang; Yao Chang
title.raw: 卷一百一十六 載記第十六 姚弋仲 姚襄 姚萇 Volume 116 Records 16: Yao Yizhong; Yao Xiang; Yao Chang

sentences.zh: 姚弋仲 姚襄 姚萇

translations.literal: Yao Yizhong; Yao Xiang; Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Yao Yizhong, his son Yao Xiang, and his son Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 姚弋仲，南安赤亭羌人也。

translations.literal: Yao Yizhong was a Qiang man from Chiting in Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong belonged to the Qiang people of Chiting in Nan'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 其先有虞氏之苗裔。

translations.literal: His ancestors were descendants of the Youyu clan.
translations.idiomatic: His line claimed descent from the legendary house of Youyu.

sentences.zh: 禹封舜少子於西戎，世為羌酋。

translations.literal: Yu enfeoffed Shun's youngest son among the western Rong; for generations they were Qiang chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Yu enfeoffed Shun's youngest son in the western borderlands, and his heirs for generations headed Qiang tribes.

sentences.zh: 其後燒當雄於洮、罕之間，七世孫填虞，漢中元末寇擾西州，為楊虛侯馬武所敗，徙出塞。

translations.literal: Later Shaodang grew powerful between Tao and Han; his seventh-generation descendant Tian Yu, late in Han's Zhongyuan era, raided and disturbed the western provinces, was defeated by Marquis Yangxu Ma Wu, and was moved beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Shaodang branch dominated the Tao and Han riverlands; seven generations after him Tian Yu ravaged the western commanderies at the close of Han's Zhongyuan reign until Ma Wu, Marquis of Yangxu, broke him and drove his people past the frontier.

sentences.zh: 虞九世孫遷那率種人內附，漢朝嘉之，假冠軍將軍、西羌校尉、歸順王，處之于南安之赤亭。

translations.literal: Tian Yu's ninth-generation descendant Qian Na led his people to submit inward; Han praised this, appointed him acting Champion General, Colonel of the Western Qiang, King of Guishun, and settled them at Chiting in Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Nine generations down, Qian Na brought his clans in from the steppe; the Han court rewarded him with acting Champion General, colonelcy over the western Qiang, the kingship of Guishun, and a grant of land at Chiting in Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 那玄孫柯回為魏鎮西將軍、綏戎校尉、西羌都督。

translations.literal: Na's great-grandson Ke Hui served Wei as General Who Guards the West, Colonel Who Pacifies the Rong, and Chief Commander of the Western Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Na's great-grandson Ke Hui became Wei's western guardian general, colonel who pacified the Rong, and overseer of the western Qiang hosts.

sentences.zh: 回生弋仲，少英毅，不營產業，唯以收恤為務，眾皆畏而親之。

translations.literal: Ke Hui's son was Yizhong; in youth he was heroic and resolute, engaged in no estate-building, and applied himself solely to gathering and relieving others; all feared yet grew intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Hui fathered Yizhong—bold and stern even young, indifferent to hoarding fields or wealth, bent on sheltering and aiding others until men both dreaded and loved him.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之亂，東徙榆眉，戎夏繈負隨之者數萬，自稱護西羌校尉、雍州刺史、扶風公。

translations.literal: When catastrophe struck in the Yongjia era, he moved east to Yumei; several tens of thousands of Rong and Han followed carrying children on their backs, and he styled himself Colonel of the Western Qiang, Inspector of Yongzhou, and Duke of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Amid the Yongjia disaster he shifted east to Yumei at the head of tens of thousands of tribesmen and Chinese who bore infants on their backs; he proclaimed himself colonel of the western Qiang, inspector of Yongzhou, and duke of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 劉曜之平陳安也，以弋仲為平西將軍，封平襄公，邑之於隴上。

translations.literal: When Liu Yao pacified Chen An, he appointed Yizhong General Who Pacifies the West, enfeoffed him Duke of Pingxiang, and granted him a fief on Longshang.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yao crushed Chen An, he named Yizhong general who pacifies the west, raised him to duke of Pingxiang, and invested him with lands along the Long plateau.

sentences.zh: 及石季龍克上邽，弋仲說之曰：「明公握兵十萬，功高一時，正是行權立策之日。

translations.literal: When Shi Jilong took Shanggui, Yizhong urged him: "My lord commands a hundred thousand men; your merit towers over the age—this is exactly the moment to wield authority and lay plans.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shi Hu seized Shanggui, Yizhong pressed him: "You hold a hundred thousand blades and overshadow every rival—now is the hour to seize initiative and set policy.

sentences.zh: 隴上多豪，秦風猛勁，道隆後服，道洿先叛，宜徙隴上豪強，虛其心腹，以實畿甸。

translations.literal: Longshang teems with stalwarts; Qin manners are fierce—where the way ascends late they submit, where it sinks they rebel first; you ought to move Longshang's powerful houses, hollow their heartlands, and thicken the capital region."
translations.idiomatic: The Long uplands breed fierce notables in the blunt Qin mold—they yield only when fortune smiles and mutiny when it falters. Relocate those magnates, gut their heart territory, and settle their strength around the throne."

sentences.zh: 」季龍納之，啟勒以弋仲行安西將軍、六夷左都督。

translations.literal: " Jilong accepted this, reported to Le, and appointed Yizhong acting General Who Pacifies the West and Left Commander-in-Chief of the Six Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Hu accepted the plan, relayed it to Shi Le, and gave Yizhong acting rank as general who pacifies the west and left commander over the six Yi peoples.

sentences.zh: 後晉豫州刺史祖約奔於勒，勒禮待之，弋仲上疏曰：「祖約殘賊晉朝，逼殺太后，不忠於主，而陛下寵之，臣恐奸亂之萌，此其始矣。

translations.literal: Later Jin's Inspector of Yuzhou Zu Yue fled to Le; Le treated him courteously. Yizhong memorialized: "Zu Yue cruelly injured Jin, forced the empress dowager to death, and was disloyal to his sovereign, yet Your Majesty favors him—I fear the seed of treason begins here.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin's Yuzhou inspector Zu Yue bolted to Shi Le, Le welcomed him with honors. Yizhong protested in writing: "Zu Yue butchered the Jin court, hounded an empress dowager to her death, and betrayed his lord—yet you indulge him; I see the first shoot of rebellion."

sentences.zh: 」勒善之，後竟誅約。

translations.literal: " Le approved and later executed Zu Yue after all.
translations.idiomatic: Le conceded the point and eventually put Zu Yue to death.

sentences.zh: 勒既死，季龍執權，思弋仲之言，遂徙秦、雍豪傑于關東。

translations.literal: After Le died, Jilong seized power, recalled Yizhong's counsel, and moved the notable families of Qin and Yong east of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le died, Shi Hu took the reins, remembered Yizhong's advice, and uprooted the great clans of Qin and Yong into the eastern plain.

sentences.zh: 弋仲率部眾數萬遷於清河，拜奮武將軍、西羌大都督，封襄平縣公。

translations.literal: Yizhong led his following of several tens of thousands and relocated to Qinghe; he was appointed General Who Rouses Might, Grand Commander of the Western Qiang, and enfeoffed Duke of Xiangping county.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong marched tens of thousands down to Qinghe, received appointment as general who rouses might and grand commander of the western Qiang, and took the county dukedom of Xiangping.

sentences.zh: 及季龍廢石弘自立，弋仲稱疾不賀。

translations.literal: When Jilong deposed Shi Hong and elevated himself, Yizhong pleaded illness and offered no congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: After Hu cast aside Shi Hong and seized the throne himself, Yizhong stayed away under cover of sickness and sent no ritual praise.

sentences.zh: 季龍累召之，乃赴，正色謂季龍曰：「奈何把臂受託而反奪之乎！

translations.literal: Jilong summoned him repeatedly before he came; with stern countenance he said to Jilong: "How can you clasp arms in trust and then seize it away!
translations.idiomatic: Hu called him again and again until he appeared; facing him squarely Yizhong demanded, "How do you embrace a dying man's charge with one hand and rip it away with the other?

sentences.zh: 」季龍憚其強正而不之責。

translations.literal: " Jilong feared his unyielding integrity and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: " Shi Hu, intimidated by that granite honesty, swallowed the rebuke.

sentences.zh: 遷持節、十郡六夷大都督、冠軍大將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to credential-bearing inspector, Grand Commander-in-Chief of ten commanderies and the Six Yi, and Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: They raised him to credential-bearing inspector, supreme commander over ten commanderies and the six Yi hosts, and champion general.

sentences.zh: 性清儉鯁直，不修威儀，屢獻讜言，無所回避，季龍甚重之。

translations.literal: By nature he was spare, frugal, blunt, and upright; he cultivated no imposing bearing, repeatedly offered blunt counsel without evasion, and Jilong greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Spare, blunt, and allergic to pomp, he spoke unwelcome truth until Hu learned to weigh every word he uttered.

sentences.zh: 朝之大議，靡不參決，公卿亦憚而推下之。

translations.literal: In every great court debate he joined the decision; even the ministers feared him and yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Every weighty policy passed through his judgment; grandees stepped down a notch rather than cross him.

sentences.zh: 武城左尉，季龍寵姬之弟也，曾擾其部，弋仲執尉，數以迫脅之狀，命左右斬之。

translations.literal: The left commandant of Wucheng was the younger brother of Jilong's favorite concubine; he once molested Yizhong's troops. Yizhong seized the commandant, rehearsed his acts of coercion, and ordered attendants to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: The left captain of Wucheng—brother to one of Hu's favorite ladies—had harassed Yizhong's men; Yizhong arrested him, listed his extortion, and had him executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 尉叩頭流血，左右諫，乃止。

translations.literal: The commandant kowtowed until blood flowed; those beside him remonstrated, and only then did Yizhong stop.
translations.idiomatic: The man battered his brow on the floor until it bled; aides pleaded until Yizhong stayed the blade.

sentences.zh: 其剛直不回，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His severity and refusal to bend were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Every anecdote told the same story—an old warrior who would not bend.

sentences.zh: 季龍末，梁犢敗李農于滎陽，季龍大懼，馳召弋仲。

translations.literal: Near the end of Jilong's reign Liang Du defeated Li Nong at Xingyang; Jilong was terrified and urgently summoned Yizhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Hu's closing years Liang Du shattered Li Nong outside Xingyang; panic sent couriers racing for Yizhong.

sentences.zh: 弋仲率其部眾八千餘人屯於南郊，輕騎至鄴。

translations.literal: Yizhong led more than eight thousand followers to camp south of the suburbs and rode light to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He brought eight thousand warriors to the southern outskirts and galloped into Ye with a slim escort.

sentences.zh: 時季龍病，不時見弋仲，引入領軍省，賜其所食之食。

translations.literal: At the time Jilong was ill and did not promptly receive him; he was led into the Army Inspector's office and given food from the ruler's table.
translations.idiomatic: Too sick for an immediate audience, Hu lodged him in the Army Inspector's compound and sent the imperial dishes.

sentences.zh: 弋仲怒不食，曰：「召我擊賊，豈來覓食邪！

translations.literal: Yizhong angrily refused to eat, saying: "You summoned me to strike rebels—did you mean me to come begging food!
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong refused the tray in disgust: "You called me to kill bandits, not to freeload a royal supper!

sentences.zh: 我不知上存亡，若一見，雖死無恨。

translations.literal: I do not know whether the sovereign still lives; let me see him once and, though I die, I shall harbor no regret.
translations.idiomatic: I hear nothing of the throne—grant one glimpse of your lord and I can die content.

sentences.zh: 」左右言之，乃引見。

translations.literal: " Those beside the throne spoke of this, and he was then granted audience.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants relayed the ultimatum and the sick emperor finally admitted him.

sentences.zh: 弋仲數季龍曰：「兒死來愁邪？

translations.literal: Yizhong rebuked Jilong: "Are you grieving because your sons died?
translations.idiomatic: Face to face he snapped at Hu: "So your boys are dead and that is what gnaws at you?

sentences.zh: 乃至於疾！

translations.literal: That it has brought you to illness!
translations.idiomatic: You have actually sickened yourself over it!

sentences.zh: 兒小時不能使好人輔相，至令相殺。

translations.literal: When your sons were young you failed to give them good assistants, until they slew one another.
translations.idiomatic: While they were boys you surrounded them with rogues instead of steady ministers—look how they cut each other down.

sentences.zh: 兒自有過，責其下人太甚，故反耳。

translations.literal: The sons had faults of their own, yet you blamed their subordinates too harshly, hence they rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: They were guilty enough, but you scourged their followers past endurance—that is why they rose.

sentences.zh: 汝病久，所立兒小，若不差，天下必亂。

translations.literal: You have been ill long; the heir you established is still small; if you do not recover, the realm will surely fall into chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Your sickness lingers and the boy you named is still a child—if you fail to rally, the empire will tear apart.

sentences.zh: 當宜憂此，不煩憂賊也。

translations.literal: You ought to worry over that, not fret over bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Worry about the succession, not field thieves.

sentences.zh: 犢等因思歸之心，共為奸盜，所行殘賊，此成擒耳。

translations.literal: Liang Du and his ilk harbor hearts longing for home; together they commit villainy and robbery and conduct themselves with cruelty—these are captives already within grasp.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Liang Du are homesick mutineers whose cruelty marks them as doomed—bagging them is trifling.

sentences.zh: 老羌請效死前鋒，使一舉而了。

translations.literal: This old Qiang begs to die on the vanguard and settle them in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Let this grey Qiang spend his life on the front rank—I will finish them at a blow."

sentences.zh: 」弋仲性狷直，俗無尊卑皆汝之，季龍恕而不責，於坐授使持節、侍中、征西大將軍，賜以鎧馬。

translations.literal: " Yizhong's nature was blunt; toward high and low alike he said "you"; Jilong forgave him without blame and at the feast invested him credential-bearing palace attendant and General Who Conquers the West, gifting armor and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt to everyone regardless of rank, he addressed lords and servants alike as "you"; Hu swallowed the insult and, still feasting, named him attendant-in-ordinary with credentials, general who conquers the west, and handed him mail and mounts.

sentences.zh: 弋仲曰：「汝看老羌堪破賊以不？

translations.literal: Yizhong said: "Do you suppose this old Qiang can break rebels?
translations.idiomatic: He barked, "Tell me—does this old Qiang still look fit to crush dogs?

sentences.zh: 」於是貫鉀跨馬於庭中，策馬南馳，不辭而出，遂滅梁犢。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he donned armor, mounted his horse in the courtyard, spurred south without bidding farewell, went out, and destroyed Liang Du.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he belted on lamellar armor, vaulted into the saddle in the courtyard, bolted south without leave, and rode Liang Du down for good.

sentences.zh: 以功加劍履上殿，入朝不趨，進封西平郡公。

translations.literal: For his merit he received sword and shoes in the hall, exemption from the hurried court pace, and advancement to Duke of Xiping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His reward was privilege to bear sword and shoes in audience, walk court without trotting, and promotion to duke of Xiping commandery.

sentences.zh: 冉閔之亂，弋仲率眾討閔，次於混橋。

translations.literal: During Ran Min's turmoil Yizhong led troops against Min and halted at Hun Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Ran Min plunged the north into civil war, Yizhong marched to oppose him and drew up at Hun Bridge.

sentences.zh: 石祗僭號于襄國，以弋仲為右丞相，待以殊禮。

translations.literal: Shi Zhi assumed title at Xiangguo and appointed Yizhong right chancellor, treating him with extraordinary ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhi declared himself emperor at Xiangguo and named Yizhong chief minister on the right with honors beyond the statute.

sentences.zh: 祗與閔相攻，弋仲遣其子襄救祗，戒襄曰：「汝才十倍于閔，若不梟擒，不須復見我也。

translations.literal: Zhi and Min attacked each other; Yizhong sent his son Xiang to rescue Zhi, instructing Xiang: "Your talent surpasses Min's tenfold—if you fail to capture him, do not face me again.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhi and Min tore at each other, Yizhong dispatched Xiang to relieve Zhi with a vow: "You outclass Ran Min tenfold—bring his head or stay away."

sentences.zh: 」襄擊閔于常盧澤，大破之而歸。

translations.literal: " Xiang attacked Min at Changlu Marsh, shattered him, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang caught Ran Min at Changlu Marsh, broke his army, and rode home.

sentences.zh: 弋仲怒襄之不擒閔也，杖之一百。

translations.literal: Yizhong was furious that Xiang had not captured Min and flogged him one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Furious that Xiang let Min escape, Yizhong had him thrashed a hundred blows.

sentences.zh: 弋仲部曲馬何羅博學有文才，張豺之輔石世也，背弋仲歸豺，豺以為尚書郎。

translations.literal: Among Yizhong's followers Ma Heluo was learned and literary; when Zhang Cao aided Shi Shi he abandoned Yizhong for Cao, who appointed him Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Heluo in Yizhong's ranks was a scholar; when Zhang Cao propped up Shi Shi he defected to become Cao's secretariat draftsman.

sentences.zh: 豺敗，復歸，咸勸殺之。

translations.literal: When Cao fell he returned; all urged killing him.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao collapsed he crawled back, and voices clamored for his execution.

sentences.zh: 弋仲曰：「今正是招才納奇之日，當收其力用，不足害也。

translations.literal: Yizhong said: "Now is precisely the time to recruit talent and admit the unusual; we ought to harness his strength—he is not worth harming.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong replied, "These are hours for gathering odd talents—put his pen to use; he is harmless."

sentences.zh: 」以為參軍。

translations.literal: " He was appointed adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Heluo was enrolled as staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 其寬恕如此。

translations.literal: His forgiveness was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the reach of his mercy.

sentences.zh: 弋仲有子四十二人，常戒諸子曰：「吾本以晉室大亂，石氏待吾厚，故欲討其賊臣以報其德。

translations.literal: Yizhong had forty-two sons and often warned his sons: "I originally acted because the Jin house fell into chaos and the Shi clan treated me generously; hence I wished to punish their traitorous ministers to repay that virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-two sons heard his standing lecture: "I drew sword because Jin collapsed and the Shis favored me—I meant to purge their traitors and settle that debt.

sentences.zh: 今石氏已滅，中原無主，自古以來未有戎狄作天子者。

translations.literal: Now the Shi are destroyed and the Central Plain lacks a ruler; never from antiquity has a Rong or Di become Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Shis are ash and the heartland has no king—never has a steppe lord seized the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 我死，汝便歸晉，當竭盡臣節，無為不義之事。

translations.literal: When I die, submit to Jin and exhaust every duty of a minister—commit no unrighteous deed.
translations.idiomatic: When I die, bend the knee to Jin, serve as faithful ministers, and touch nothing dishonorable."

sentences.zh: 」乃遣使請降。

translations.literal: " He then sent envoys to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: With that he dispatched envoys offering submission.

sentences.zh: 永和七年，拜弋仲使持節、六夷大都督、都督江、淮諸軍事、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、大單于，封高陵郡公。

translations.literal: In Yonghe's seventh year he was appointed credential-bearing inspector, Grand Commander-in-Chief of the Six Yi, commander-in-chief of Jiang and Huai military affairs, General of Chariots and Cavalry, honors equal to the Three Offices, Grand Shanyu, and enfeoffed Duke of Gaoling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghe seventh year invested him with credentials as commander of the six Yi, governor of Jiang-Huai armies, chariot-and-cavalry general, parity with the Three Dukes, grand Shanyu, and duke of Gaoling commandery.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒，時年七十三。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died the next year at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 子襄之入關也，為苻生所敗，弋仲之柩為生所得，生以王禮葬之于天水冀縣。

translations.literal: When Xiang entered the Pass he was defeated by Fu Sheng; Yizhong's coffin fell into Sheng's hands, and Sheng buried it by royal rites in Ji county of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiang's thrust into Guanzhong collapsed before Fu Sheng; Sheng seized Yizhong's bier and buried it at Ji in Tianshui with kingly ceremony.

sentences.zh: 萇僭位，追諡曰景元皇帝，廟號始祖，墓曰高陵，置園邑五百家。

translations.literal: When Chang usurped the throne he posthumously honored him as Emperor Jingyuan with temple title First Ancestor, tomb name Gaoling, and established an administrative hamlet of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chang seized the throne he canonized his father as Emperor Jingyuan, First Ancestor, with tomb name Gaoling and five hundred households to tend the graves.

sentences.zh: 襄字景國，弋仲之第五子也。

translations.literal: Xiang's courtesy name was Jingguo; he was Yizhong's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang, whose courtesy name was Jingguo, was the fifth son of Yizhong.

sentences.zh: 年十七，身長八尺五寸，臂垂過膝，雄武多才藝，明察善撫納，士眾愛敬之，咸請為嗣。

translations.literal: At seventeen he stood eight chi five cun tall; his arms hung past his knees; he was heroic and martial and multiply talented; perceptive and skilled at winning men; soldiers loved and revered him—all petitioned that he be heir.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he measured eight and a half chi, arms reaching below the knee; fierce, versatile, shrewd, and magnetic, he won every warrior's devotion until they begged to make him successor.

sentences.zh: 弋仲弗許，百姓固請者日有千數，乃授之以兵。

translations.literal: Yizhong refused; commoners who firmly petitioned numbered in the thousands daily; then he entrusted him with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong refused until thousands besieged him daily with the plea—only then did he hand Xiang a command.

sentences.zh: 石祗僭號，以襄為使持節、驃騎將軍、護烏丸校尉、豫州刺史、新昌公。

translations.literal: When Shi Zhi assumed title he appointed Xiang credential-bearing inspector, General Who Spreads Might, Colonel of the Wuhuan, Inspector of Yuzhou, and Duke of Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhi's coup brought Xiang credentials as general who spreads might, Wuhuan colonel, Yuzhou inspector, and duke of Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 晉遣使拜襄持節、平北將軍、并州刺史、即丘縣公。

translations.literal: Jin dispatched envoys to appoint Xiang credential-bearing inspector, General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Bingzhou, and Duke of Jiuqiu county.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court answered with credentials naming him general who pacifies the north, Bingzhou inspector, and duke of Jiuqiu county.

sentences.zh: 弋仲死，襄秘不發喪，率戶六萬南攻陽平、元城、發幹，皆破之，殺掠三千餘家，屯於碻磝津。

translations.literal: When Yizhong died Xiang concealed the death, led sixty thousand households south to attack Yangping, Yuancheng, and Fagan, broke them all, killed and plundered more than three thousand households, and camped at Qiaoao Ford.
translations.idiomatic: At his father's death Xiang hid the coffin, marched sixty thousand households south against Yangping, Yuancheng, and Fagan, stormed each, slaughtered and looted three thousand families, and halted at Qiaoao crossing.

sentences.zh: 以太原王亮為長史，天水尹赤為司馬，略陽伏子成為左部帥，南安斂岐為右部帥，略陽黑那為前部帥，強白為後部帥，太原薛贊、略陽王權翼為參軍。

translations.literal: He appointed Wang Liang of Taiyuan chief clerk, Yin Chi of Tianshui marshal, Fu Zicheng of Lüeyang commander of the left wing, Lian Qi of Nan'an commander of the right wing, Heina of Lüeyang commander of the van, Qiang Bai commander of the rear, Xue Zan of Taiyuan and Quan Yi of Lüeyang as advisers.
translations.idiomatic: His staff took shape with Wang Liang of Taiyuan as chief clerk, Yin Chi of Tianshui as marshal, Fu Zicheng and Heina of Lüeyang flanking the van and wings, Lian Qi of Nan'an on the right, Qiang Bai covering the rear, and Xue Zan with Quan Yi as advisers.

sentences.zh: 南至滎陽，始發喪行服。

translations.literal: South of Xingyang he began mourning and donned mourning garb.
translations.idiomatic: Only south of Xingyang did he publish the death and put on hemp.

sentences.zh: 與高昌、李曆戰于麻田，馬中流矢死，賴其弟萇以免。

translations.literal: He fought Gao Chang and Li Li at Matian; his horse was struck by a stray arrow and died; he survived thanks to his younger brother Chang.
translations.idiomatic: At Matian he clashed with Gao Chang and Li Li; a stray bolt slew his mount and only his brother Chang pulled him clear.

sentences.zh: 晉處襄於譙城，遣五弟為任，單騎度淮，見豫州刺史謝尚于壽春。

translations.literal: Jin housed Xiang at Qiao city, sent five younger brothers as hostages, and he rode alone across the Huai to meet Jin's Inspector of Yuzhou Xie Shang at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Jin quartered him at Qiao, demanded five brothers as pledges, and watched him ride solo across the Huai to parley with Yuzhou inspector Xie Shang in Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 尚命去仗衛，幅巾以待之，一面交款，便若平生。

translations.literal: Shang ordered away weapons and guards and waited in plain headcloth as for a friend; one meeting forged intimacy as if lifelong.
translations.idiomatic: Shang dismissed arms and escorts, received him bareheaded like an old friend, and after one evening they talked like brothers.

sentences.zh: 襄少有高名，雄武冠世，好學博通，雅善談論，英濟之稱著于南夏。

translations.literal: From youth Xiang bore a lofty reputation; martial prowess crowned his age; fond of learning and broadly versed; graceful in discourse; the epithet "heroic champion" flourished south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Even young he carried fame as the foremost warrior-scholar of the generation—learned, eloquent, and known across the south as the consummate champion.

sentences.zh: 中軍將軍、揚州刺史殷浩憚其威名，乃因襄諸弟，頻遣刺客殺襄，刺客皆推誠告實，襄待之若舊。

translations.literal: Central Army General and Yangzhou Inspector Yin Hao dreaded his renown; through Xiang's brothers he repeatedly sent assassins against Xiang; the assassins every time pledged sincerity and truth; Xiang treated them as of old.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao, commanding the central army at Yangzhou, feared that reputation and fed killers through Xiang's brothers—yet each assassin confessed and Xiang welcomed them like honored guests.

sentences.zh: 浩潛遣將軍魏憬率五千餘人襲襄，襄乃斬憬而並其眾。

translations.literal: Hao secretly sent General Wei Jing with more than five thousand men to raid Xiang; Xiang thereupon beheaded Jing and absorbed his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hao then slipped General Wei Jing forward with five thousand men; Xiang struck first, took Jing's head, and drafted his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 浩愈惡之，乃使將軍劉啟守譙，遷襄于梁國蠡台，表授梁國內史。

translations.literal: Hao hated him the more and therefore sent General Liu Qi to hold Qiao, moved Xiang to Lihao Terrace in Liang state, and memorialized appointment as administrator of Liang state.
translations.idiomatic: The snub deepened Hao's spite: he planted Liu Qi on Qiao, shunted Xiang to Lihao terrace in Liang commandery, and tabled him as interior minister there.

sentences.zh: 襄遣權翼詣浩，浩曰：「姚平北每舉動自由，豈所望也。

translations.literal: Xiang sent Quan Yi to Hao; Hao said: "General Yao the northern pacifier acts wholly on his own—is that what we hoped for?
translations.idiomatic: Xiang dispatched Quan Yi to parley; Hao snapped, "Your General Yao does exactly as he pleases—is that the vassal we bargained for?

sentences.zh: 」翼曰：「將軍輕納奸言，自生疑貳，愚謂猜嫌之由，不在於彼。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "The general lightly believed slander and bred mistrust himself; I foolishly suppose the source of suspicion lies not with him.
translations.idiomatic: " Quan Yi answered, "You swallow rumor and nurse your own doubts—the rift is not of his making.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「姚君縱放小人，盜竊吾馬，王臣之體固若是乎？

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Lord Yao indulges petty men who steal my horses—is this how a royal minister behaves?
translations.idiomatic: " Hao pressed, "He shelters thieves who lifted my mounts—is that courtly discipline?

sentences.zh: 」翼曰：「將軍謂姚平北以威武自強，終為難保，校兵練眾，將懲不恪，取馬者欲以自衛耳。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "The general supposed Lord Yao the northern pacifier relied on force and could never be trusted; he drilled troops to punish laxity; those who took horses sought only self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi replied, "You assumed Yao would bully neighbors with arms, so he trained men to restore order—the horse thieves were guarding themselves.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「何至是也。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "How could it reach this?
translations.idiomatic: " Hao sneered, "Surely not.

sentences.zh: 」浩遣謝萬討襄，襄逆擊破之。

translations.literal: " Hao dispatched Xie Wan against Xiang; Xiang met him and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Xie Wan; Xiang intercepted and shattered the column.

sentences.zh: 浩甚怒，會聞關中有變，浩率眾北伐，襄乃要擊浩于山桑，大敗之，斬獲萬計，收其資仗。

translations.literal: Hao was furious; when word came of turmoil in Guanzhong Hao led troops on a northern expedition; Xiang ambushed Hao at Shansang, routed him utterly, killed and captured by the myriad account, and seized his baggage and arms.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Hao marched north on news from Guanzhong; Xiang sprang the trap at Shansang, cut him to pieces, stacked ten thousand heads, and captured wagons and weapons.

sentences.zh: 使兄益守山桑壘，復如淮南。

translations.literal: He left his elder brother Yi to hold the Shansang fort and again went to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He stationed elder brother Yi on the Shansang wall and doubled back toward Huainan.

sentences.zh: 浩遣劉啟、王彬之伐山桑，襄自淮南擊滅之，鼓行濟淮，屯於盱眙，招掠流人，眾至七萬，分置守宰，勸課農桑，遣使建鄴，罪狀殷浩，並自陳謝。

translations.literal: Hao sent Liu Qi and Wang Binzhi to attack Shansang; Xiang came from Huainan and destroyed them, beat drums crossing the Huai, camped at Xuyi, recruited and plundered displaced people until his host reached seventy thousand, divided officers to hold territory, urged farming and mulberry, sent envoys to Jianye indicting Yin Hao while stating his own apology.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao ordered Liu Qi and Wang Binzhi against Shansang, Xiang swept up from Huainan, annihilated them, drummed across the Huai, anchored at Xuyi, swept refugees until seventy thousand answered his banner, appointed magistrates, pushed tillage and silk, and sent word to Jianye accusing Yin Hao yet confessing his own trespass.

sentences.zh: 流人郭斁等千餘人執晉堂邑內史劉仕降於襄，朝延大震，以吏部尚書周閔為中軍將軍，緣江備守。

translations.literal: More than a thousand displaced persons led by Gu Yi seized Jin's interior administrator of Tangyi, Liu Shi, and surrendered him to Xiang; the court trembled greatly and appointed Minister of Personnel Zhou Min central army general to guard the river line.
translations.idiomatic: When wanderers under Gu Yi seized Tangyi's interior minister Liu Shi and handed him to Xiang, the court reeled and named Zhou Min of the personnel ministry general of the central army to brace the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 襄將佐部眾皆北人，咸勸襄北還。

translations.literal: Xiang's staff and following were all northerners; all urged Xiang to return north.
translations.idiomatic: Every adviser and soldier hailed from the north and clamored to march home.

sentences.zh: 襄方軌北引，自稱大將軍、大單于，進攻外黃，為晉邊將所敗。

translations.literal: Xiang drove north in ordered columns, styled himself Grand General and Grand Shanyu, attacked Waihuang, and was defeated by Jin border generals.
translations.idiomatic: He formed ranks for a northern march, proclaimed himself grand general and grand Shanyu, struck Waihuang, and stumbled against Jin frontier troops.

sentences.zh: 襄收散卒而勤撫恤之，於是復振。

translations.literal: He gathered scattered soldiers and diligently comforted them; thereby he revived.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied stragglers and tended them patiently until his army breathed again.

sentences.zh: 乃據許昌，將如河東以圖關右，自許遂攻洛陽，逾月不克。

translations.literal: Thereupon he occupied Xuchang; he intended to go to Hedong to plan Guanzhong; from Xu he attacked Luoyang but could not take it within a month.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing Xuchang, he aimed at Hedong and the greater Guanzhong design; from there he threw columns at Luoyang yet failed for a full month.

sentences.zh: 其長史王亮諫襄曰：「公英略蓋天下，士眾思效力命，不可損威勞眾，守此孤城。

translations.literal: His chief clerk Wang Liang remonstrated with Xiang: "Your lordship's strategy overshadows the realm; soldiers long to spend their lives for you—you cannot waste prestige and tire the host guarding this lone city.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Wang Liang warned him: "Your genius outmatches the age and men ache to die for you—do not squander awe besieging one stubborn town.

sentences.zh: 宜還河北，以弘遠略。

translations.literal: You ought to return north of the Yellow River to enlarge distant designs."
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw north of the river and reopen the wider campaign."

sentences.zh: 」襄曰：「洛陽雖小，山河四塞之固，亦是用武之地。

translations.literal: " Xiang said: "Though Luoyang is small, its mountains and rivers form four barriers—it too is ground for arms.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiang answered, "Luoyang looks small yet sits locked by river and hill—it remains a battlefield worth holding.

sentences.zh: 吾欲先據洛陽，然後開建大業。

translations.literal: I desire first to seize Luoyang, then open and establish great enterprise."
translations.idiomatic: " I mean to take Luoyang first, then unfold the larger enterprise."

sentences.zh: 」俄而亮卒，襄哭之甚慟，曰：「天將不欲成吾事乎？

translations.literal: " Shortly Liang died; Xiang wept exceedingly bitterly and said: "Does Heaven refuse to complete my affair?
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Liang died soon after; Xiang mourned wildly and cried, "Does Heaven deny my purpose?

sentences.zh: 王亮舍我去也！」

translations.literal: Wang Liang has left me!"
translations.idiomatic: Has Wang Liang abandoned me?"

sentences.zh: 晉征西大將軍桓溫自江陵伐襄，戰于伊水北，為溫所敗，率麾下數千騎奔於北山。

translations.literal: Jin's General Who Conquers the West Huan Wen campaigned from Jiangling against Xiang; they fought north of the Yi River; he was defeated by Wen and led several thousand riders of his command to flee to the northern hills.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen marched from Jiangling; their clash along the Yi ended in rout; Xiang bolted into the northern hills with a few thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 其夜，百姓棄妻子隨襄者五千餘人，屯據陽鄉，赴者又四千餘戶。

translations.literal: That night commoners who abandoned wives and children to follow Xiang numbered more than five thousand; they encamped at Yangxiang and another four thousand-plus households hurried to join.
translations.idiomatic: That night over five thousand souls forsook families to trail him; they dug in at Yangxiang while four thousand more households raced after.

sentences.zh: 襄前後敗喪數矣，眾知襄所在，輒扶老攜幼賓士而赴之。

translations.literal: Though Xiang had suffered repeated defeats, whenever the crowd learned where Xiang was they would support the old and lead the young, rushing headlong to reach him.
translations.idiomatic: Even after repeated disasters, word of his camp drew refugees who carried elders and tugged children in desperate haste to his banner.

sentences.zh: 時或傳襄創重不濟，溫軍所得士女莫不北望揮涕。

translations.literal: At times word spread that Xiang's wounds were grave and he would not recover; among the men and women captured by Wen's army there was none who did not gaze north and wipe tears.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors flew that Xiang's wounds would kill him; every civilian Wen's troops had taken turned north, weeping openly.

sentences.zh: 其得物情如此。

translations.literal: Thus did he win the feelings of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the devotion he inspired among common folk.

sentences.zh: 先是，弘農楊亮歸襄，襄待以客禮。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Liang of Hongnong had joined Xiang; Xiang treated him with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yang Liang of Hongnong had come over; Xiang received him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 後奔桓溫，溫問襄於亮，亮曰：「神明器宇，孫策之儔，而雄武過之。

translations.literal: Later he fled to Huan Wen; Wen asked Liang about Xiang, and Liang said: "In divine bearing and breadth of mind he matches Sun Ce, yet exceeds him in martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang later bolted to Huan Wen, Wen asked his verdict: "He has Sun Ce's magnetism and stature—only his battlefield edge is greater."

sentences.zh: 」其見重如是。

translations.literal: " Thus was he esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the respect he commanded.

sentences.zh: 萇字景茂，弋仲第二十四子也。

translations.literal: Chang's courtesy name was Maomao; he was Yizhong's twenty-fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang, courtesy Maomao, ranked twenty-fourth among Yizhong's sons.

sentences.zh: 少聰哲，多權略，廓落任率，不修行業，諸兄皆奇之。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and wise, full of stratagem, broad-minded and forthright, cultivated no formal vocation, and his elder brothers all marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and calculating even young, candid and unfettered, he cared nothing for textbook virtue—yet every older brother sensed something singular.

sentences.zh: 隨襄征伐，每參大謀。

translations.literal: He accompanied Xiang on campaigns and always joined the great plans.
translations.idiomatic: He rode with Xiang on every expedition and sat in on the councils.

sentences.zh: 襄之寇洛陽也，夢萇服袞衣，升御坐，諸酋長皆侍立，旦謂將佐曰：「吾夢如此，此兒志度不恆，或能大起吾族。

translations.literal: When Xiang raided Luoyang he dreamed that Chang wore imperial robes, ascended the throne, and all chieftains stood attendance; at dawn he told his officers: "My dream was thus—this boy's ambition is not ordinary; perhaps he can greatly exalt our clan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Luoyang strike Xiang dreamed Chang robed as emperor, mounting the dais while tribal heads lined the hall; at dawn he confided, "That dream tells me the lad's aims run deep—he may yet lift our house."

sentences.zh: 」襄之敗于麻田也，馬中流矢死，萇下馬以授襄，襄曰：「汝何以自免？

translations.literal: " When Xiang was defeated at Matian, a stray arrow killed his horse; Chang dismounted and gave it to Xiang; Xiang said: "How will you yourself escape?
translations.idiomatic: After Matian, when a bolt slew Xiang's mount, Chang handed over his own horse; Xiang demanded, "What becomes of you then?"

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「但令兄濟，豎子安敢害萇！

translations.literal: " Chang said: "Only let my elder brother win free—would some wretch dare harm Chang!
translations.idiomatic: " Chang shot back, "Once you ride clear, no stray soldier touches me!"

sentences.zh: 」會救至，俱免。

translations.literal: " Relief arrived in time; both escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Reinforcements arrived; both walked away.

sentences.zh: 及襄死，萇率諸弟降于苻生。

translations.literal: When Xiang died, Chang led his younger brothers to surrender to Fu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiang fell, Chang brought the brothers in under Fu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 苻堅以萇為揚武將軍。

translations.literal: Fu Jian appointed Chang General Who Spreads Might.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian named him general who spreads might.

sentences.zh: 曆左衛將軍，隴東、汲郡、河東、武都、武威、巴西、扶風太守，甯、幽、兗三州刺史，復為揚武將軍，步兵校尉，封益都侯。

translations.literal: He successively served as general of the Left Guard, prefect of Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Weiba, Brazil, and Fufeng, inspector of Ning, You, and Yan, again General Who Spreads Might, colonel of infantry, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed through left guard general, a chain of western prefectures—Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Weiba, Brazil, Fufeng—three provincial inspectorships, a second tour as general who spreads might, colonel of foot, and the marquisate of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 為堅將，累有大功。

translations.literal: As Jian's general he repeatedly earned great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jian he stacked victory upon victory.

sentences.zh: 初，萇隨楊安伐蜀，嘗晝寢水旁，上有神光煥然，左右咸異之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chang followed Yang An's Shu expedition, he once napped by day beside the water; divine light blazed above him and all beside him wondered.
translations.idiomatic: Once, napping riverside during Yang An's Shu campaign, a nimbus flared over him and every attendant gaped.

sentences.zh: 及苻堅寇晉，以萇為龍驤將軍、督益、梁州諸軍事，謂萇曰：「朕本以龍驤建業，龍驤之號未曾假人，今特以相授，山南之事一以委卿。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian invaded Jin he appointed Chang Dragon-General and supervisor of military affairs in Yi and Liang, saying to Chang: "I originally founded the enterprise as Dragon-General; I have never lent that title—now I specially confer it; all matters south of the mountains I entrust to you.
translations.idiomatic: For the Jin invasion Jian named Chang dragon-general for Yi-Liang armies and told him, "I rose under that banner and never gave it away—now it is yours; everything south of the ranges rests with you."

sentences.zh: 」堅左將軍竇沖進曰：「王者無戲言，此將不祥之征也，惟陛下察之。

translations.literal: " Jian's general of the left Dou Chong stepped forward: "A king has no jesting words—this commission is an ill omen; may Your Majesty examine it.
translations.idiomatic: " Left general Dou Chong warned, "Thrones do not joke—that title is a bad augury; reconsider."

sentences.zh: 」堅默然。

translations.literal: " Jian fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Jian answered with silence.

sentences.zh: 堅既敗於淮南，歸長安，慕容泓起兵叛堅。

translations.literal: After Jian was defeated at Huainan he returned to Chang'an; Murong Hong rose in rebellion against him.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan broke him; he fled back to Chang'an as Murong Hong mutinied.

sentences.zh: 堅遣子叡討之，以萇為司馬。

translations.literal: Jian sent his son Rui to punish him and appointed Chang marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Jian dispatched Prince Rui against Hong and made Chang his marshal.

sentences.zh: 為泓所敗，叡死之。

translations.literal: Hong defeated them and Rui died in the engagement.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hong shattered the army and Prince Rui died on the field.

sentences.zh: 萇遣龍驤長史趙都詣堅謝罪，堅怒，殺之。

translations.literal: Chang sent Dragon-General chief clerk Zhao Du to Jian to apologize; Jian in rage executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang sent chief clerk Zhao Du to apologize; Jian killed the envoy in fury.

sentences.zh: 萇懼，奔於渭北，遂如馬牧。

translations.literal: Chang feared and fled to the north bank of the Wei, then went to the horse pastures.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Chang bolted beyond the Wei and made for the government studs.

sentences.zh: 西州豪族尹詳、趙曜、王欽盧、王欽盧、牛雙、狄廣、張乾等率五萬餘家，咸推萇為盟主。

translations.literal: Western province magnates Yin Xiang, Zhao Yao, Wang Qinlu, Wang Qinlu, Niu Shuang, Di Guang, Zhang Qian and others led more than fifty thousand households, all pushing Chang as covenant chief.
translations.idiomatic: Great families west of the pass—Yin Xiang, Zhao Yao, Wang Qinlu twice named in the text, Niu Shuang, Di Guang, Zhang Qian—marched fifty thousand households forward and thrust the alliance staff on Chang.

sentences.zh: 萇將距之，天水尹緯說萇曰：「今百六之數既臻，秦亡之兆已見，以將軍威靈命世，必能匡濟時艱，故豪傑驅馳，咸同推仰。

translations.literal: Chang was about to refuse; Yin Wei of Tianshui urged Chang: "The fatal cycle of one hundred six has arrived; omens of Qin's fall already appear; by your majesty's awesome mandate you can surely rescue this crisis; hence heroes gallop in and alike urge you on.
translations.idiomatic: Chang hesitated until Yin Wei of Tianshui argued, "The calendar's doom-year is here and Qin is finished—only your aura can steady the age; that is why every magnate begs you to lead."

sentences.zh: 明公宜降心從議，以副群望，不可坐觀沈溺而不拯救之。

translations.literal: My lord ought to humble your heart and heed counsel to match the host's hope—you cannot sit watching them drown without rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Bow to their plea instead of watching them sink—you cannot idle while the realm drowns."

sentences.zh: 」萇乃從緯謀，乙太元九年自稱大將軍、大單于、萬年秦王，大赦境內，年號白雀，稱制行事。

translations.literal: " Chang then followed Wei's plan; in Taiyuan's ninth year he styled himself Grand General, Grand Shanyu, Prince of Wannian of Great Qin, amnestied his territory, era name White Sparrow, and issued orders as regent.
translations.idiomatic: He took the advice: in the ninth year of Taiyuan he proclaimed himself grand general, grand Shanyu, and Prince of Wannian under the Great Qin banner, declared era White Sparrow, amnestied his zone, and ruled by decree.

sentences.zh: 以天水尹詳、南安龐演為左右長史，南安姚晃、尹緯為左右司馬，天水狄伯支、焦虔、梁希、龐魏、任謙為從事中郎，姜訓、閻遵為掾屬，王據、焦世、蔣秀、尹延年、牛雙、張乾為參軍，王欽盧、姚方成、王破虜、楊難、尹嵩、裴騎、趙曜、狄廣、黨刪等為帥。

translations.literal: He appointed Yin Xiang of Tianshui and Pang Yan of Nan'an left and right chief clerks, Yao Huang and Yin Wei of Nan'an left and right marshals, Di Bozhi, Jiao Qian, Liang Xi, Pang Wei, Ren Qian of Tianshui as advisory aides, Jiang Xun and Yan Zun as staffers, Wang Ju, Jiao Shi, Jiang Xiu, Yin Yannian, Niu Shuang, Zhang Qian as advisers, Wang Qinlu, Yao Fangcheng, Wang Polu, Yang Nan, Yin Song, Pei Qi, Zhao Yao, Di Guang, Dang Shan and others as commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Staff filled out with Yin Xiang and Pang Yan as chief clerks, Yao Huang and Yin Wei as marshals, a corps of Tianshui aides—Di Bozhi, Jiao Qian, Liang Xi, Pang Wei, Ren Qian—scribes Jiang Xun and Yan Zun, advisers Wang Ju through Zhang Qian, and column leaders from Wang Qinlu to Dang Shan.

sentences.zh: 時慕容沖與苻堅相攻，眾甚盛。

translations.literal: At the time Murong Chong and Fu Jian attacked each other; Chong's host was very large.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong and Fu Jian were locked in war and Chong's numbers swelled.

sentences.zh: 萇將西上，恐沖遏之，乃遣使通和，以子崇為質於沖，進屯北地，厲兵積粟，以觀時變。

translations.literal: Chang intended to march west and feared Chong would block him; he therefore sent envoys seeking peace, sent his son Chong as hostage to Chong, advanced and camped at Beidi, sharpened weapons and hoarded grain to watch how times shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Marching west meant slipping past Chong, so Chang sued for truce, handed son Chong as hostage, dug in at Beidi, stacked grain and arms, and waited.

sentences.zh: 苻堅先徙晉人李祥等數千戶于敷陸，至是，降於萇，北地、新平、安定羌胡降者十餘萬戶。

translations.literal: Fu Jian had earlier moved several thousand households of Jin people such as Li Xiang to Fulu; now they surrendered to Chang; Qiang and Hu of Beidi, Xinping, and Anding who submitted exceeded one hundred thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had relocated Jin families like Li Xiang to Fulu; they now opened their gates to Chang, joined by more than a hundred thousand tribal households across Beidi, Xinping, and Anding.

sentences.zh: 堅率諸將攻之，不能克。

translations.literal: Jian led generals against him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian threw columns at him and could not break the line.

sentences.zh: 萇聞容慕沖攻長安，議進趨之計，群下咸曰：「宜先據咸陽以制天下。

translations.literal: When Chang heard that Murong Chong was attacking Chang'an, he debated plans to hurry there; his subordinates all said: "You ought first to seize Xianyang to control the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Murong Chong was storming Chang'an, he debated a dash to the capital; aides insisted, "Secure Xianyang first and the realm follows."

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「燕因懷舊之士而起兵，若功成事捷，咸有東歸之思，安能久固秦川！

translations.literal: " Chang said: "Yan rose through men homesick for the east; if they succeed, all will long to return east—how could they long hold the Qin plain!
translations.idiomatic: " Chang countered, "Yan rides eastern nostalgia; victory would only send them home—they cannot stay on the Qin plain!"

sentences.zh: 吾欲移兵嶺北，廣收資實，須秦弊燕回，然後垂拱取之。

translations.literal: I desire to shift troops north of the ranges, broadly gather supplies, wait until Qin is exhausted and Yan withdraws, then take all with folded hands.
translations.idiomatic: " I will slide north of the divide, stockpile strength, and when Qin breaks and Yan marches away, scoop the prize without a blow.

sentences.zh: 兵不血刃，坐定天下，此卞莊得二之義也。

translations.literal: Weapons undrawn, sitting to settle the world—this is the sense of Bian Zhuang seizing two prey.
translations.idiomatic: That is Bian Zhuang letting two tigers wound each other—bloodless triumph."

sentences.zh: 」堅甯朔將軍宋方率騎三千從雲中將赴長安，萇自貳縣要破之，方單馬奔免，其司馬田晃率眾降萇。

translations.literal: Jian's General Who Quiets the North Song Fang led three thousand cavalry from Yunzhong intending to reach Chang'an; Chang intercepted him from Er county and broke him; Fang alone fled for life; his marshal Tian Huang led the host to surrender to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian's general Song Fang raced three thousand riders from Yunzhong toward Chang'an, Chang ambushed him at Er; Fang escaped alone while marshal Tian Huang handed over the column.

sentences.zh: 萇遣諸將攻新平，克之，因略地至安定，嶺北諸城盡降之。

translations.literal: Chang sent generals to assault Xinping, took it, then raided as far as Anding; all cities north of the ranges surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: His generals stormed Xinping, swept to Anding, and every town north of the divide capitulated.

sentences.zh: 時苻堅為慕容沖所逼，走入五將山。

translations.literal: At the time Fu Jian was pressed by Murong Chong and fled into Mount Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong harried Jian until he bolted into the Wujiang hills.

sentences.zh: 沖入長安。

translations.literal: Chong entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chong walked into Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 堅司隸校尉權翼、尚書趙遷、大鴻臚皇甫覆、光祿大夫薛贊、扶風太守段鏗等文武數百人奔於萇。

translations.literal: Jian's metropolitan investigator Quan Yi, Minister Zhao Qian, Grand Master of Ceremonies Huangfu Fu, palace counselor Xue Zan, prefect of Fufeng Duan Keng, and several hundred civil and military officers fled to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of Jian's officials—Quan Yi, Zhao Qian, Huangfu Fu, Xue Zan, Duan Keng—crossed to Chang's camp.

sentences.zh: 萇遣驍騎將軍吳忠率騎圍堅，萇如新平。

translations.literal: Chang sent Swift Cavalry General Wu Zhong to surround Jian with horse troops; Chang himself went to Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: Chang ordered Wu Zhong's riders to ring Jian while he rode to Xinping.

sentences.zh: 俄而忠執堅，送之。

translations.literal: Shortly Zhong seized Jian and sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wu Zhong took Jian alive and shipped him in.

sentences.zh: 慕容沖遣其車騎大將軍高蓋率眾五萬來伐，戰于新平南，大破之，蓋率麾下數千人來降，拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Murong Chong sent his chariot and horse grand general Gao Gai with fifty thousand to attack; they fought south of Xinping; Chang utterly defeated him; Gai led several thousand of his command to surrender and was appointed supernumerary palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's general Gao Gai marched fifty thousand south of Xinping and collapsed; Gai brought thousands over and won a supernumerary attendant's tile.

sentences.zh: 沖既率眾東下，長安空虛。

translations.literal: After Chong led his host eastward downriver, Chang'an stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chong swept downstream, Chang'an hollowed out.

sentences.zh: 盧水郝奴稱帝于長安，渭北盡應之。

translations.literal: Hao Nu of the Lu River styled himself emperor at Chang'an; all north of the Wei answered him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu-water chieftain Hao Nu crowned himself in the capital while the northern Wei shore rose in his name.

sentences.zh: 扶風王驎有眾數千，保據馬嵬。

translations.literal: Wang Lin of Fufeng had several thousand followers and held Mawei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin of Fufeng gripped Mawei with a few thousand men.

sentences.zh: 奴遣弟多攻驎。

translations.literal: Nu sent his younger brother Duo to attack Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Nu sent brother Duo against him.

sentences.zh: 萇伐驎，破之，驎走漢中。

translations.literal: Chang campaigned against Lin, broke him, and Lin fled to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Chang smashed Wang Lin, who bolted for Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 執多而進攻奴，降之。

translations.literal: He seized Duo and advanced to attack Nu, who surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He took Duo, wheeled on Hao Nu, and forced his capitulation.

sentences.zh: 乙太元十一年萇僭即皇帝位於長安，大赦，改元曰建初，國號大秦，改長安曰常安。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of the Taiyuan era Chang usurped the imperial throne at Chang'an, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Jianchu, adopted the state title Great Qin, and renamed Chang'an with a new official spelling meaning enduring peace yet pronounced like the old capital name.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyuan eleventh year Chang took the throne at Chang'an, declared amnesty, adopted era Jianchu and dynastic title Great Qin, and rechristened the metropolis with a court spelling that punned on Chang'an while invoking lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 立妻虵氏為皇后，子興為皇太子，置百官。

translations.literal: He established Lady She as empress, son Xing as crown prince, and installed the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Lady She became empress, Yao Xing crown prince, and the bureaucracy filled out.

sentences.zh: 自謂以火德承苻氏木行，服色如漢氏承周故事。

translations.literal: He claimed that by virtue of fire he succeeded Fu's wood phase, with robes and colors following Han's precedent of inheriting Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He argued his fire virtue followed Fu's wood in the five-phase cycle and dressed the court after Han's Zhou succession ritual.

sentences.zh: 徙安定五千餘戶于長安。

translations.literal: He moved more than five thousand households from Anding to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He relocated five thousand Anding families into the capital.

sentences.zh: 以弟征虜緒為司隸校尉，鎮長安。

translations.literal: He appointed younger brother the General Who Conquers Captives, Xu, metropolitan investigator to guard Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Yao Xu, general who conquers captives, stayed as metropolitan investigator in the capital.

sentences.zh: 萇如安定，擊平涼胡金熙、鮮卑沒奕於，大破之。

translations.literal: Chang went to Anding, struck the Pingliang Hu Jin Xi and the Xianbei Moyifu, and shattered them.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Anding, crushed Jin Xi among the Pingliang Hu and Moyifu of the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 遂如秦州，與苻堅秦州刺史王統相持，天水屠各、略陽羌胡應萇者二萬餘戶，統懼，乃降。

translations.literal: He then went to Qinzhou and locked horns with Wang Tong, Jian's inspector of Qinzhou; two-plus ten thousand households of Tujue Luochuan in Tianshui and Qiang Hu of Lüeyang answered Chang; Tong feared and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At Qinzhou he faced Wang Tong until droves—Tujue herders in Tianshui, Qiang and Hu in Lüeyang—swelled his rolls; Tong yielded.

sentences.zh: 因饗將士於上邽，南安人古成詵進曰：「臣州人殷地險，俊傑如林，用武之國也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he feasted officers at Shanggui; Gu Chengshan of Nan'an advanced and said: "My province's people are prosperous and the terrain perilous; heroes stand thick as a forest—it is a land suited to arms.
translations.idiomatic: At the Shanggui feast Gu Chengshan of Nan'an urged, "Our land is rich, rugged, and crowded with talent—made for war."

sentences.zh: 王秦州不能收拔賢才，三分鼎足，而坐玩珠玉，以至於此。

translations.literal: Wang the inspector of Qinzhou could not gather worthy men to stand as one leg of a tripod and instead idly played with pearls and jade, until it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet inspector Wang toyed with gems instead of forging a tripod—look where it led."

sentences.zh: 陛下宜散秦州金帛以施六軍，旌賢表善以副鄙州之望。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to scatter Qinzhou's gold and silk to supply the six armies, raise banners for worthies and display goodness to answer my province's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: Spend Qinzhou's treasure on the armies, loud-hail the virtuous, and you honor what we hoped for."

sentences.zh: 」萇善之，擢為尚書郎。

translations.literal: " Chang approved and promoted him to Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Chang agreed and kicked Shen upstairs to the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 拜弟碩德都督隴右諸軍事、征西將軍、秦州刺史，領護東羌校尉，鎮上邽。

translations.literal: He appointed younger brother Shuode commander of Longyou military affairs, General Who Conquers the West, inspector of Qinzhou, concurrently colonel who guards the eastern Qiang, guarding Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Yao Shuode took Longyou command, general who conquers the west, Qinzhou inspectorship, eastern Qiang colonelcy, and the Shanggui garrison.

sentences.zh: 萇還安定，修德政，布惠化，省非急之費，以救時弊，閭閻之士有豪介之善者，皆顯異之。

translations.literal: Chang returned to Anding, cultivated virtuous government, spread kindness, cut expenditures not urgently needed to relieve current ills, and for village scholars who showed heroic integrity he displayed distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Anding he trimmed waste, pushed humane rule, and singled out village stalwarts with blunt integrity.

sentences.zh: 萇復如秦州，為苻登所敗，語在《登傳》。

translations.literal: Chang again went to Qinzhou and was defeated by Fu Deng—the fuller narrative is recorded in Fu Deng's biography.
translations.idiomatic: His renewed thrust into Qinzhou broke against Fu Deng; the campaign is told at length in Fu Deng's biography.

sentences.zh: 以其太子興鎮長安，而與登相距。

translations.literal: He stationed crown prince Xing at Chang'an while he faced Deng at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: He left crown prince Xing holding the capital while he shadowboxed Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 登馮翊太守蘭犢與苻師奴離貳，慕容永攻之，犢遣使請救。

translations.literal: Deng's prefect of Fengyi Lan Niu split from Fu Shinu; Murong Yong attacked him; Niu sent envoys begging rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Niu of Fengyi broke with Fu Shinu under Murong Yong's hammer and cried for aid.

sentences.zh: 萇將赴救，尚書令姚旻、左僕射尹緯等言於萇曰：「苻登近在瓦亭，陛下未宜輕舉。

translations.literal: Chang was about to march to save them; Minister over the Masses Yao Min, left servant Yin Wei and others said to Chang: "Fu Deng is near Watting; Your Majesty ought not lightly move.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yao Min and Yin Wei warned, "Fu Deng lurks at Watting—do not ride out rashly."

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「登遲重少決，每失時機，聞吾自行，正當廣集兵資，必不能輕軍深入。

translations.literal: " Chang said: "Deng is sluggish and seldom decisive; always he misses the hour; hearing that I myself march, he will only broadly gather soldiers and supplies—certainly he cannot lightly drive deep with an army.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang retorted, "Deng is slow; news of my personal march will send him hoarding supplies—he will never plunge deep."

sentences.zh: 兩月之間，足可克此三豎，吾事必矣。

translations.literal: Within two months it suffices to capture these three striplings; my enterprise is assured.
translations.idiomatic: Two months will cage those three upstarts—then the board is mine."

sentences.zh: 」遂師次於渥源。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the army halted at Woyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The host camped at Woyuan.

sentences.zh: 師奴率眾來距，大戰，敗之，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: Shinu led troops to oppose him; they fought a great battle; Chang defeated him and took all his host captive.
translations.idiomatic: Shinu barred the road; Chang crushed him and bagged the army.

sentences.zh: 又擒蘭犢，收其士馬。

translations.literal: He also seized Lan Niu and gathered his soldiers and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Niu fell too, men and mounts included.

sentences.zh: 萇乃掘苻堅屍，鞭撻無數，裸剝衣裳，薦之以棘，坎土而埋之。

translations.literal: Chang thereupon exhumed Fu Jian's corpse, flogged it countless times, stripped the garments bare, laid it on brambles, and buried it in a pit of earth.
translations.idiomatic: Then he dug up Fu Jian, lashed the corpse, stripped it, heaped thorns atop it, and shoveled dirt.

sentences.zh: 慕容永征西將軍王宣率眾降萇。

translations.literal: Murong Yong's General Who Conquers the West Wang Xuan led troops to surrender to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuan, Yong's western conqueror, brought his column over.

sentences.zh: 初，關西雄傑以苻氏既終，萇雄略命世，天下之事可一旦而定。

translations.literal: Earlier, heroes west of the pass thought that with Fu spent and Chang's stratagem commanding the age, matters under Heaven could be settled in a morning.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fu seemed finished, western stalwarts assumed Chang could settle the realm overnight.

sentences.zh: 萇既與苻登相持積年，數為登所敗，遠近咸懷去就之計，唯征虜齊難、冠軍徐洛生、輔國劉郭單、冠威彌姐婆觸、龍驤趙惡地、鎮北梁國兒等守忠不貳，並留子弟守營，供繼軍糧，身將精卒，隨萇征伐。

translations.literal: After Chang locked horns with Fu Deng year on year and repeatedly suffered Deng's defeats, near and far alike harbored plans to leave or join; only General Who Conquers Captives Qi Nan, Champion Xu Luosheng, Assistant to the State Liu Guodan, Champion Might Mizijie Poluo, Dragon-General Zhao Edi, General Who Guards the North Liang Guoer and others kept faith undivided, all leaving sons to guard camps, supplying successive army grain, themselves leading picked troops to follow Chang on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Years of stalemate and Deng's victories sapped loyalty—yet Qi Nan, Xu Luosheng, Liu Guodan, Mizijie Poluo, Zhao Edi, Liang Guoer and a handful kept the pledge, sons guarding baggage trains while fathers rode with Chang.

sentences.zh: 時諸營既多，故號萇軍為大營，大營之號自此始也。

translations.literal: Because camps were many at the time, Chang's army was called the Great Camp—the title Great Camp begins here.
translations.idiomatic: So many stockades clustered that men dubbed Chang's host the Great Camp—the nickname begins here.

sentences.zh: 時天大雪，萇下書深自責罰，散後宮文綺珍寶以供戎事，身食一味，妻不重彩。

translations.literal: At the time heaven sent heavy snow; Chang issued an edict blaming himself deeply, scattered rear-palace silks and treasures to supply military affairs, ate only single dishes himself, and his wife wore no doubled colors.
translations.idiomatic: Blizzard weather brought a self-scourging edict: palace silks went to the armies, the ruler ate one dish, the empress shed bright dyes.

sentences.zh: 將帥死王事者，加秩二等，士卒戰沒，皆有褒贈。

translations.literal: For commanders who died in royal service he raised rank two grades; for soldiers fallen in battle there were all commendations and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Fallen generals jumped two ranks posthumously; common soldiers won pensions.

sentences.zh: 立太學，禮先賢之後。

translations.literal: He established the Imperial Academy and honored the descendants of former worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the academy and ennobled sage-descendants.

sentences.zh: 敦煌索盧曜請刺苻登，萇曰：「卿以身徇難，將為誰乎？

translations.literal: Suo Luyao of Dunhuang asked to assassinate Fu Deng; Chang said: "You offer your body for peril—on whose behalf?
translations.idiomatic: Suo Luyao of Dunhuang volunteered to murder Fu Deng; Chang asked, "You stake your life—for whom?"

sentences.zh: 」曜曰：「臣死之後，深以友人隴西辛暹仰托。

translations.literal: " Luyao said: "After my death I deeply entrust my friend Xin Xian of Longxi to your care.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "If I fall, keep an eye on my friend Xin Xian of Longxi."

sentences.zh: 」萇遣之。

translations.literal: " Chang sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang let him go.

sentences.zh: 事發，為登所殺，萇以暹為騎都尉。

translations.literal: When the affair broke he was killed by Deng; Chang appointed Xian colonel of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The plot failed and Deng killed him; Chang made Xin a cavalry colonel.

sentences.zh: 登進逼安定，諸將勸萇決戰，萇曰：「與窮寇競勝，兵家之下。

translations.literal: Deng advanced pressing Anding; generals urged Chang to decisive battle; Chang said: "To vie for victory with a cornered foe is the low tactic of the art of war.
translations.idiomatic: As Deng pressed Anding, generals bayed for battle; Chang said, "Trading blows with a trapped enemy is the meanest stratagem."

sentences.zh: 吾將以計取之。

translations.literal: " I intend to take him by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: " I will snare him by craft."

sentences.zh: 」於是留其尚書令姚旻守安定，夜襲登輜重於大界，克之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he left Minister over the Masses Yao Min holding Anding and night-raided Deng's baggage at Dajie, taking it.
translations.idiomatic: He left Yao Min on Anding and slipped by night into Deng's Dajie train, seizing the wagons.

sentences.zh: 諸將或欲因登駭亂擊之，萇曰：「登眾雖亂，怒氣猶盛，未可輕也。

translations.literal: Some generals wished to strike Deng while he was shaken and disorderly; Chang said: "Though Deng's host is disorderly, angry qi is still strong—it cannot be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Aides wanted to strike the chaos; Chang refused: "Their ranks waver but their rage runs hot—wait."

sentences.zh: 」遂止。

translations.literal: " He stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He held the line.

sentences.zh: 萇以安定地狹，且逼苻登，使姚碩德鎮安定，徙安定千餘家安于陰密，遣弟征南靖鎮之。

translations.literal: Chang because Anding's territory was narrow and Deng pressed close made Yao Shuode guard Anding, moved more than a thousand households of Anding to settle at Yinmi, and sent younger brother the General Who Conquers the South Jing to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Anding felt tight against Deng, so Shuode stayed put while a thousand families shifted to Yinmi under brother Yao Jing's southern command.

sentences.zh: 立社稷于長安。

translations.literal: He established the altars of soil and grain at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He raised the state altars in the capital.

sentences.zh: 百姓年七十有德行者，拜為中大夫，歲賜牛酒。

translations.literal: Commoners seventy years old possessing virtue and conduct were appointed grand masters of the fifth grade and yearly gifted oxen and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous septuagenarians became honorary grandees with yearly oxen and wine.

sentences.zh: 尹緯、姚晃謂古成詵曰：「苻登窮寇，歷年未滅，奸雄鴟峙，所在糾扇，夷夏皆貳，將若之何？

translations.literal: Yin Wei and Yao Huang spoke to Gu Chengshan: "Fu Deng is a cornered foe yet years have not destroyed him; villains perch like owls everywhere rallying; Yi and Xia alike waver—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Yin Wei and Yao Huang pressed Gu Chengshan: "Years later Deng still breathes; predators flock on every side; Chinese and tribesmen hedge—what next?"

sentences.zh: 」詵曰：「主上權略無方，信賞必罰，賢能之士，咸懷樂推，豈慮大業不成，氐賊不滅乎！

translations.literal: " Chengshan said: "Our lord's stratagem knows no bound; trust rewards and certain punishments move all worthy men to joyful allegiance—why worry the great enterprise will not succeed or the Di bandit will not perish!
translations.idiomatic: " Chengshan retorted, "Clear rewards and sure punishments win every able man—why fear the Di outlaw!"

sentences.zh: 」緯曰：「登窮寇未滅，奸雄所在扇合，吾等寧無懼乎？

translations.literal: " Wei said: "Deng the cornered foe is not yet destroyed; villains everywhere rally—ought we not fear?
translations.idiomatic: " Yin Wei shot back, "Yet rebels still gather—should we sleep easy?"

sentences.zh: 」詵曰：「三秦天府之國，主上十分已有其八。

translations.literal: " Chengshan said: "The three Qins are Heaven's storehouse; our lord already holds eight tenths.
translations.idiomatic: " Chengshan answered, "The triple Qin heartland is heaven's granary—our lord holds eight shares in ten."

sentences.zh: 今所在可慮者，苻登、楊定、雷惡地耳，自餘瑣瑣，焉足論哉！

translations.literal: Those worth worrying over now are Fu Deng, Yang Ding, and Lei Edi alone; the rest are petty—how are they worth discourse!
translations.idiomatic: Only Fu Deng, Yang Ding, and Lei Edi merit worry; the rest are gnats!"

sentences.zh: 然惡地地狹眾寡，不足為憂。

translations.literal: Yet Edi's territory is narrow and host small—not sufficient for worry.
translations.idiomatic: And Lei Edi rules a scrap of ground—hardly worth a thought."

sentences.zh: 苻登藉烏合犬羊，偷存假息，料其智勇，非至尊之匹。

translations.literal: Fu Deng borrows a flock of crow-struck dogs and sheep, stealing breath to survive; gauge his wit and courage—he is no peer for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng clings to a mongrel host—measure his wit and nerve and he cannot rival you.

sentences.zh: 霸王之起，必有驅除，然後克定大業。

translations.literal: When a hegemon-king rises, there must be clearance driving away foes; only then can the great enterprise be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Every founding conqueror sweeps rivals aside before the realm locks shut.

sentences.zh: 昔漢、魏之興也，皆十有餘年，乃能一同於海內，五六年間未為久也。

translations.literal: In antiquity the rises of Han and Wei each took more than ten years before they could unify within the seas; five or six years is not long.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei needed more than a decade to unite the realm—a handful of years is nothing.

sentences.zh: 主上神略內明，英武外發，可謂無敵於天下耳，取登有餘力。

translations.literal: Our lord is divinely wise within and majestically martial without—one may say without peer under Heaven; taking Deng leaves strength to spare.
translations.idiomatic: Your insight within and thunder without leave no rival under Heaven—Fu Deng will cost you little effort.

sentences.zh: 願布德行仁，招賢納士，厲兵秣馬，以候天機。

translations.literal: I pray you spread virtue, practice kindness, summon worthies, fatten horses and sharpen blades, and await Heaven's moment.
translations.idiomatic: Spread humane rule, recruit talent, hone armies, and watch for fate's opening.

sentences.zh: 如其鴻業不成者，詵請腰斬以謝明公。

translations.literal: If perchance the grand enterprise fails, Shen begs to be cut at the waist to apologize to my lord.
translations.idiomatic: If your enterprise stalls, take my torso in two—I will answer with my life.

sentences.zh: 」緯言之於萇，萇大悅，賜詵爵關內侯。

translations.literal: " Wei reported this to Chang; Chang was greatly pleased and enfeoffed Shen as marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Wei relayed it; Chang glowed and raised Shen to marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 雷惡地率眾降萇，拜為鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: Lei Edi led his host to surrender to Chang and was appointed General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Edi brought his column in and earned general who guards the east.

sentences.zh: 魏褐飛自稱大將軍、沖天王，率氐胡數萬人攻安北姚當城於杏城，雷惡地應之，攻鎮東姚漢得于李潤。

translations.literal: Wei Hefei styled himself Grand General and Heaven-Rushing King and led tens of thousands of Di and Hu to assault General Who Guards the North Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng; Lei Edi answered him and attacked General Who Guards the East Yao Hande at Lirun.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hefei proclaimed himself grand general and Heaven-Rushing King, threw Di and Hu tens of thousands deep against Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng; Lei Edi pitched in against Yao Hande at Lirun.

sentences.zh: 萇議將討之，群臣咸曰：「陛下不憂六十里苻登，乃憂六百里褐飛？

translations.literal: Chang debated campaigning against them; all ministers said: "Your Majesty does not worry over Fu Deng sixty li away, yet worries over Wei Hefei six hundred li away?
translations.idiomatic: Ministers protested, "Fu Deng sits sixty li off while Hefei marches six hundred—why fear the distant bandit?"

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「登非可卒殄，吾城亦非登所能卒圖。

translations.literal: " Chang said: "Deng cannot be crushed in haste; neither can my cities be swiftly mapped by Deng.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang answered, "Deng will not fall overnight; neither will he swallow my towns at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 惡地多智，非常人也。

translations.literal: Edi is full of stratagem—no ordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Edi is cunning—no common foe.

sentences.zh: 南引褐飛，東結董成，甘言美說以成奸謀，若得杏城、李潤，惡地據之，控制遠近，相為羽翼，長安東北非復吾有。

translations.literal: Southward he draws Hefei, eastward he binds Dong Cheng—sweet words and fair speeches complete treacherous designs; if Xingcheng and Lirun fall and Edi holds them, controlling far and near and lending each other wings, the northeast of Chang'an will no longer be ours.
translations.idiomatic: He ropes Hefei on the south and Dong Cheng on the east—smooth talk masks a trap; let him park on Xingcheng and Lirun and the northeast gate of Chang'an slides from our grasp."

sentences.zh: 」於是潛軍赴之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he secretly marched against them.
translations.idiomatic: Chang slipped columns toward them.

sentences.zh: 萇時眾不滿二千，褐飛、惡地眾至數萬，氐胡赴之者首尾不絕。

translations.literal: At the time Chang's host numbered fewer than two thousand; Hefei's and Edi's reached tens of thousands; Di and Hu flocking to them came without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Chang mustered under two thousand against tens of thousands; tribal recruits stretched endlessly.

sentences.zh: 萇每見一軍至，輒有喜色。

translations.literal: Whenever Chang saw another army arrive he showed pleased color.
translations.idiomatic: Each fresh enemy column lit his face with satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 群下怪而問之，萇曰：「今同惡相濟，皆來會集，吾得乘勝席捲，一舉而覆其巢穴，東北無復餘也。

translations.literal: His staff wondered and questioned him; Chang said: "Now men of shared wickedness aid each other—all come to gather; I can ride victory and roll them up, overturn their nests in one blow; nothing will remain northeast.
translations.idiomatic: He explained, "They flock together—one whirlwind sweep empties their nests."

sentences.zh: 」褐飛等以萇兵少，盡眾來攻。

translations.literal: " Hefei and others because Chang's troops were few brought their entire host to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking him weak, Hefei threw every spear forward.

sentences.zh: 萇固壘不戰，示之以弱，潛遣子崇率騎數百，出其不意，以乘其後。

translations.literal: Chang held fast behind ramparts and declined battle, displaying weakness; secretly he sent son Chong with several hundred horse to burst unexpectedly upon their rear.
translations.idiomatic: Chang hugged his walls, feigned frailty, then slipped Chong around with hundreds of riders.

sentences.zh: 褐飛兵擾亂，萇遣鎮遠王超、平遠譚亮率步騎擊之，褐飛眾大潰，斬褐飛及首級萬餘。

translations.literal: Hefei's troops fell into confusion; Chang sent General Who Guards the Distance Wang Chao and Pacifies the Distance Tan Liang with foot and horse to strike them; Hefei's host utterly collapsed; they beheaded Hefei and more than ten thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Chong broke their rear; Wang Chao and Tan Liang chopped the column to pieces; Hefei's head joined ten thousand others.

sentences.zh: 惡地請降，萇待之如初。

translations.literal: Edi begged surrender; Chang treated him as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Edi capitulated and Chang welcomed him as before.

sentences.zh: 惡地每謂人曰：「吾自言智勇所施，足為一時之傑。

translations.literal: Edi often told others: "I myself declare that where wit and courage apply, I suffice as a hero of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Edi boasted, "My wit and nerve should crown an age."

sentences.zh: 校數諸雄，如吾之徒，皆應跨據一方，獸嘯千里。

translations.literal: Measured against the heroes, men like me ought each to stride astride a quarter and roar like beasts across a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Peers like me deserve realms of our own—we should rule plains like roaring beasts."

sentences.zh: 遇姚公智力摧屈，是吾分也。

translations.literal: Meeting Lord Yao my wit and strength were broken—that is my appointed share.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Yao broke me—that was fate."

sentences.zh: 」惡地猛毅清肅，不可幹以非義，嶺北諸豪皆敬憚之。

translations.literal: Edi was fierce, resolute, austere, and incorruptible—no unjust plea could sway him; all magnates north of the ranges revered and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce, upright, immune to flattery, Lei Edi cowed every upland chief.

sentences.zh: 萇命其將當城于營處一柵孔中蒔樹一根，以旌戰功。

translations.literal: Chang ordered general Dangcheng to plant one tree in a single fence hole at the camp site to signal martial merit.
translations.idiomatic: He told Yao Dangcheng to raise one victory tree in a palisade gap.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，問之，城曰：「營所至小，已廣之矣。

translations.literal: After more than a year he asked; Dangcheng said: "The camp ground was small—it has already been enlarged.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Dangcheng reported the drill yard had grown beyond the first stake."

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「少來鬥戰無如此快，以千六百人破三萬眾，國之事業，由此克舉。

translations.literal: " Chang said: "In youth I never knew fighting so swift—sixteen hundred men broke thirty thousand; the state's enterprise through this can succeed.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang crowed, "Sixteen hundred routing thirty thousand—never was war so sweet; the dynasty turns on this stroke."

sentences.zh: 小乃為奇，大何足貴！」

translations.literal: Small thus becomes marvelous—what glory is there in mere size!"
translations.idiomatic: " Small hosts win wonders—mass alone proves nothing!"

sentences.zh: 貳城胡曹寅、王達獻馬三千匹。

translations.literal: Hu of Ercheng Cao Yin and Wang Da presented three thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yin and Wang Da of Ercheng Hu delivered three thousand mounts.

sentences.zh: 以寅為鎮北將軍、并州刺史，達鎮遠將軍、金城太守。

translations.literal: Yin was appointed General Who Guards the North and inspector of Bingzhou; Da General Who Guards the Distance and prefect of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yin became northern guardian general and Bingzhou inspector; Wang Da earned distant guardian general and Jincheng prefect.

sentences.zh: 萇性簡率，群下有過，或面加罵辱。

translations.literal: Chang's nature was blunt and forthright; when subordinates erred he sometimes abused them to their faces.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt by temperament, he dressed down aides in open hall.

sentences.zh: 太常權翼言於萇曰：「陛下弘達自任，不修小節，駕馭群雄，苞羅俊異，棄嫌錄善，有高祖之量。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies Quan Yi said to Chang: "Your Majesty is magnanimous and self-trusting, cultivates no petty etiquette, reins heroes, embraces unusual talent, casts aside grudges and records goodness—you have the capacity of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi praised his Liu Bang-scale openness—riding heroes, forgiving slights.

sentences.zh: 然輕慢之風，所宜除也。

translations.literal: Yet the manner of rash contempt ought to be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Still, cure the habit of casual insult."

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「吾之性也。

translations.literal: " Chang said: "That is my nature.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang shrugged, "That is how I am."

sentences.zh: 吾於舜之美，未有片焉；

translations.literal: Toward Shun's beauties I possess not a single slice;
translations.idiomatic: Of Shun's shining virtues I claim not even a sliver;

sentences.zh: 漢祖之短，已收其一。

translations.literal: among Han Gaozu's shortcomings I already harbor one.
translations.idiomatic: yet I already mirror one of Han Gaozu's faults.

sentences.zh: 若不聞讜言，安知過也！」

translations.literal: If I did not hear blunt speech, how would I know my faults!"
translations.idiomatic: " Without candor I would never see my faults!"

sentences.zh: 南羌竇鴦率戶五千來降，拜安西將軍。

translations.literal: Southern Qiang Dou Yuan led five thousand households to surrender and was appointed General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yuan of the southern Qiang brought five thousand households and won western pacifier general.

sentences.zh: 萇下書，有復私仇者，皆誅之。

translations.literal: Chang issued an edict: whoever took private revenge was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He outlawed blood feuds on pain of death.

sentences.zh: 將吏亡滅者，各隨所親以立後，振給長育之。

translations.literal: For officers lost in destruction each followed kin to establish heirs and relief for raising them.
translations.idiomatic: Fallen officers won adopted heirs through kin lines and state stipends for orphans.

sentences.zh: 鎮東苟曜據逆萬堡，密引苻登。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the East Gou Yao held Rebel-Wan fort and secretly drew Fu Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern guardian Gou Yao gripped Rebel-Wan keeps and connived with Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 萇與登戰，敗于馬頭原，收眾復戰。

translations.literal: Chang fought Deng and was defeated at Matou Plain; he gathered troops and fought again.
translations.idiomatic: Matou Plain broke him once; he re-formed and struck again.

sentences.zh: 姚碩德謂諸將曰：「上慎于輕戰，每欲以計取之。

translations.literal: Yao Shuode told the generals: "The sovereign is cautious about light combat—always wishing to take foes by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Shuode warned, "Our lord hates rash battle—he prefers schemes."

sentences.zh: 今戰既失利，而更逼賊者，必有由也。

translations.literal: Now that combat already failed yet presses the bandits closer, there must be a reason.
translations.idiomatic: After a loss he still crowds the enemy—there is motive."

sentences.zh: 」萇聞而謂碩德曰：「登用兵遲緩，不識虛實，今輕兵直進，逕據吾東，必苟曜豎子與之連結也。

translations.literal: Hearing this Chang told Shuode: "Deng employs arms sluggishly and does not discern void from solid; now light troops advance straight and occupy our east—they must be linking with the stripling Gou Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Chang explained to Shuode, "Deng is slow; light troops seizing our east mean Gou Yao is stitching a pact."

sentences.zh: 事久變成，其禍難測。

translations.literal: If matters drag on and change completes, the calamity cannot be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: Let it fester and the peril grows unreadable."

sentences.zh: 所以速戰者，欲使豎子謀之未就，好之未深，散敗其事耳。

translations.literal: The reason for swift battle is to catch the stripling before his plot ripens and fondness deepens—scatter and wreck his affair.
translations.idiomatic: " I strike fast so Gou's intrigue never ripens."

sentences.zh: 」進戰，大敗之，登退屯於郿。

translations.literal: " He pressed the attack, utterly defeated Deng, and Deng withdrew to camp at Mei.
